answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits catch fabricated results. A real agent earns the stake back through verified tasks; a sybil swarm must tie up capital in every identity and risks losing it repeatedly. The stake is a signal, not proof of personhood: like a vine, trust grows through observed performance, while a relic of old credentials alone grants no immunity.
